title: Contrapposto Rest
imageAlt: Standing mannequin figure with weight on one leg, opposite hip and shoulder tilted, one hand resting on the hip.
tip: Put your weight on one leg and let the other relax — hips and shoulders tilt in opposite directions.
advice: Lock the knee of the standing leg softly, not hard — a fully locked knee gets tiring.
Rest a hand on the hip of the relaxed side to keep the arm stable.
Choose a fixed point on the wall for your gaze so your head returns to the same angle.

title: Overhead Stretch
imageAlt: Standing figure stretching both arms straight above the head.
tip: A long vertical line from heels to fingertips. Keep it short — raised arms tire quickly.
advice: Interlace your fingers or hold one wrist to share the load between both arms.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears; let the shoulder blades drop.
Lower the arms slightly if your hands start tingling — a small change is fine.

title: Glance Over the Shoulder
imageAlt: Figure turned three-quarters away, head looking back over the shoulder, one hand on the hip.
tip: Turn the body away and bring the head back toward the room. The twist creates instant interest.
advice: Turn mostly from the hips and ribcage; keep the neck rotation gentle.
Place the hand of the turned side on the hip to anchor the shoulders.
Pick a gaze point you can comfortably hold for the full pose.

title: Forward Lean on a Stool
imageAlt: Figure seated on a stool, leaning forward with forearms resting on the thighs.
tip: Lean forward and let your forearms rest on your thighs — the stool and legs carry the weight.
advice: Spread your feet a little wider than your hips for a stable base.
Rest your forearms rather than your elbows to avoid pressure points.
Let your head hang naturally; holding it high gets tiring over 20 minutes.

title: Floor Sit, Leaning Back
imageAlt: Figure sitting on the floor, leaning back on both hands, one knee raised.
tip: Sit on the floor, lean back on your hands and bend one knee — an open, relaxed triangle shape.
advice: Place your hands slightly turned outward to protect the wrists.
Bend one knee up to create varied shapes for the artists.
Ask for a cushion or mat so the floor stays comfortable.

title: Side Recline, Head Propped
imageAlt: Figure lying on its side, upper body raised, head propped on one hand, top knee bent.
tip: Lie on your side with your head resting on one hand. One of the most sustainable long poses.
advice: Use a cushion under the hip and under the propping elbow.
Bend the top knee forward to keep the pelvis from rolling.
If the propping arm gets heavy, rest your head on the forearm instead — mention it to the organizer.

title: Lunge and Reach
imageAlt: Figure in a forward lunge with one arm reaching far ahead and the other extended back.
tip: A strong diagonal from back foot to reaching hand. Commit fully — it only lasts a minute or two.
advice: Make the stance wide enough that you don't wobble.
Reach with intention: extend through the fingertips.
Keep it to quick gesture rounds — this is not a pose to hold.

title: Spiral Twist
imageAlt: Standing figure twisting through the torso, one arm raised high, the other low.
tip: Feet face one way, shoulders another. The spiral through the torso gives artists rhythm to chase.
advice: Plant both feet before you rotate the upper body.
Raise one arm to exaggerate the spiral; keep the other low.
Breathe out into the twist — don't hold your breath.

title: Throw
imageAlt: Figure caught mid-throw, one arm drawn back, the other extended forward.
tip: Freeze the moment just before a throw — arm drawn back, weight loaded on the back leg.
advice: Think of a real action; imagined movement reads as more convincing.
Lean the torso clearly away from the throwing direction.
Keep the stance stable enough to hold still for the whole minute.

advice: Keep a soft bend in the knees to protect the lower back.
Let your hands take some of the upper body weight.

tip: A staff or pole adds a second support point and lets you hold an elegant line for longer.
advice: Place the staff a little in front of you so you can lean into it.
Hold it at shoulder height or below; higher gets tiring.

tip: A calm, natural standing pose. Folded arms keep the shoulders relaxed and the hands still.
advice: Shift the weight to one leg, then back to centre if you need a micro-rest.
Fold the arms loosely — tight arms cut off circulation.

title: Kneeling Arch
imageAlt: Kneeling figure arching back, chest open, hands behind the head.
tip: Kneel, open the chest and tip the head back with hands behind it. Expressive — and demanding.
advice: Always kneel on a cushion or folded mat.
Arch from the upper back, not by crunching the lower back.
Come out slowly at the end; give yourself a moment before standing.

imageAlt: Figure seated on a stool with the torso turned, one leg extended, one tucked back.
tip: Sit on a stool, turn your shoulders away from your knees and tuck one leg back.
advice: Let the stool take your weight; the twist should feel easy, not forced.
Rest one hand on the stool behind you for support.
Turn the head with the shoulders to avoid neck strain.

title: Kneeling Rest
imageAlt: Figure kneeling on one knee with the other foot planted and a forearm resting on the raised knee.
tip: One knee down, one foot planted, forearm resting on the raised knee. Grounded and calm.
advice: Put a cushion under the kneeling knee.
Let the forearm rest on the raised knee rather than holding it up.
Swap sides on the next pose to give the knee a break.
